items.decision: Do not promote without clarifying insertion indices beyond current album length
findings: Raw source contains the full custom-input protocol n/index/n/identity; catalog truncation is an HTML parsing artifact, not missing original input lines.

Original bounds allow0<=index[i]<n, including index[0]>0 when the album is empty. Source does not explain whether such indices append, create gaps, or are invalid; there are no examples to disambiguate.

Catalog Python list.insert silently clamps an index beyond length; Java list.add rejects it and C++ begin()+index is invalid. These imported solutions disagree, so do not treat any as authoritative or silently impose index[i]<=i.

items.decision: Implemented in gemini-1-recovered; Linux207-case reference validation, three negative controls, independent review and four real submissions passed. See dedicated immutable batch and integration evidence; not yet deployed.
findings: Original explicitly supplies n>=1 and nonnegative integer heights, with no numeric upper bounds. int[] interface can justify a disclosed nonnegative signed32 input adaptation, not an invented small n.

Previous return-int overflow concern is not sufficient: painting each positive board vertically gives answer<=n, so the full32MiB input transport domain keeps the mathematical answer below signed32 range.
Catalog recursive minimum-scan solution is quadratic and its text incorrectly claims n is small without source evidence. Do not reuse it for full transport-domain verification.

Explore streaming monotone-stack Cartesian-tree DP with equal-height compression and zero separators. Full flat low-height arrays can have roughly16million items, so avoid allocating several n-sized arrays without a measured memory bound. Independent brute painting/interval DP required before promotion.

items.decision: Do not promote on current source evidence
findings: Goldman first sample is unreachable for its actual input; explanation silently changes the matrix.
Airbnb includes departure cell in obstacle checks; Goldman begins at the adjacent cell. Sources cannot be treated as equivalent for an obstructed start.
Neither source guarantees clear endpoints or explicitly settles a1x1 obstructed grid.
Existing Airbnb3 package publicly chooses obstructed endpoints=-1, including1x1. Its passing tests verify that chosen rule, not original-source uniqueness.
Both sources describe1..26 decoding counts but omit numeric length bounds.
decoding-string.md describes a different reversed ASCII decoding task. Its bounds cannot be borrowed.
An int return type alone does not bound input length or authorize modular arithmetic.
